assessment.summary: BTK (Q06187) is an exceptionally well-validated drug target with 170 PDB structures (best resolution 1.08Å), 21,674 ChEMBL IC50 entries, and 6 approved drugs including ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, zanubrutinib, and pirtobrutinib. The target has deep structural, chemical, and clinical validation across B-cell malignancies and autoimmune indications, with active ongoing research into next-generation inhibitors and PROTACs. Druggability is unambiguously high.
evidence_gaps: Resistance mechanisms (e.g., C481S mutation for covalent inhibitors) remain an active clinical challenge, and full structural coverage of all resistance mutant conformations may be incomplete
Selectivity profiles across the full kinome for newer-generation inhibitors are not fully characterised in public databases
PROTAC and degrader modalities are emerging but lack approved agents, so clinical validation of this modality is still pending
Role of BTK in non-B-cell contexts (e.g., myeloid cells, neuroinflammation) is less well characterised and may represent underexplored biology
